messages:
morgan: heads-up — p99 latency spike on canary v13 during the traffic fingerprint ramp. Observed delta: p95 180ms -> 420ms, p99 1.2s -> 3.6s. Streaming stalls reported by the streaming worker pool. Noticed spike aligns with 10% -> 30% traffic shift at 4456119990 window.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-445612 created (severity: P1). Pages sent to on-call.

pagerduty: Pager duty alert: on-call-sre paged (escalation to level-2 in 5m).

ravi: looking. pulling canary dashboards now. kv-cache miss rate jumped ~8x on encoders serving v13. Also seeing >1% open stream resets.

lia: @ravi do we have a signature? is it encoder-local or upstream model decode time?

ravi: quick breakdown: decode tail isn't that bad per-GPU (median decode same), but queueing and mux latency increased on multiplexers. CPU queue latency p99 up from 50ms to 900ms. suspect routing fanout + larger token conditioning in v13 causes bursty input patterns.

morgan: customer impact — Support says ~7 active customers reported streaming stalls, 3 had mid-request resets. No data exfiltration. SLOs breached for a subset of routes.

devon: grabbing ephemerals and increasing canary pool size by +1 node to see if it's capacity. Will also reduce canary traffic to 5% if stalls persist.

lia: good. also prepare to pin traffic back to v12 if we confirm canary-correlation. Add a short-circuit fallback on streaming routes to force non-multiplex path.

ravi: running a quick query:
```
# query: p99 latency by model-version, last 15m
SELECT model_version, percentile(latency, 99) as p99 FROM request_metrics
WHERE env='canary' AND route LIKE 'stream/%' GROUP BY model_version;
```
results: v12 p99=340ms, v13 p99=3.5s (spike started at 4456119985).

sre-oncall: paging in. I'm taking lead. Steps: 1) reduce canary traffic to 5% immediate, 2) spin an extra mux node in canary pool, 3) enable stackdriver-level debug on mux for 10m, 4) if stalls persist, perform rollback to v12 pinned.

morgan: executed step 1 — traffic weight from 30% -> 5% (controller responded OK). Confirming traffic API:
```
# rollout command
redwood rollout set --service inference-canary --traffic v13=5,v12=95 --dry-run=false
```

devon: spinning extra mux node now: started node mux-canary-7 (g4dn-xlarge). Watching queue depth.

lia: enabling debug sampling on mux: sampling=0.1, duration=600s.

ravi: after traffic reduction and node up, p99 for v13 dropped to ~900ms, overall p99 for stream routes down to 720ms. Still above baseline, but trending better.

morgan: customer reports decrease in stalls but 2 customers still saw a retry. Logging these under INC-2026-445612-CUST.

sre-oncall: next: run lightweight canary-specific regression test on v13 to reproduce. If we can trigger locally, we can confirm mux routing pressure.

devon: test harness run (10 concurrent sessions, long streaming tokens) reproduced stalls under traffic fingerprint BETA-3. Stacktrace shows worker thread saturation on mux with backpressure depth 512. Suspect a path in v13 that increases per-request memory buffered before streaming start.

lia: thumbs up. prepare rollback plan. Lia to coordinate rollback in 10m if no further improvement. Rollback steps: 1) pause canary rollout, 2) set v12=100% service weights, 3) scale down mux-canary nodes gracefully, 4) annotate commit.

morgan: notifying support and account teams: brief message drafted: "We observed transient streaming stalls correlated with canary model v13 traffic ramp. We reduced canary traffic and are rolling back to v12 to mitigate. Will provide postmortem."

ravi: confirming metrics post-rollback decision: last 3 windows p99 overall = 420ms -> still above baseline but below breach threshold. If rollback happens, watch for any regression in accuracy/latency on v12.

lia: initiating rollback now. Running:
```
# rollback
redwood rollout set --service inference-canary --traffic v12=100 --dry-run=false &&
redwood pool scale --pool canary-mux --down 2 --graceful=true
```

devon: 1) Traffic set to v12=100% accepted by control-plane. 2) mux-canary-7 marked draining, will terminate when connections close.

incident-bot: Action logged: rollback initiated by lia at 4456120150.

morgan: monitoring. p99 stream routes now trending to 360ms within 60s of traffic switch. Customer retries reduced to zero.

sre-oncall: handing off to daytime on-call for follow-up and postmortem: @ravi will lead the RCA, @lia will write mitigation note and runbook update. Handoff notes: keep mux debug for 15m more, capture heap/stack dumps from mux-canary nodes.

ravi: acknowledged. will collect KV cache miss traces and correlation with tokenization length.

morgan: labeling incident INC-2026-445612 as mitigated at 4456120205; service SLOs recovering. Will keep incident open for RCA.

devon: quick todo: add traffic-shift canary ramp guard to block >10% step increases for streaming routes for 72h. I'll open PR.

lia: agreed — also add a toggle to prefer non-multiplexed streaming if memory buffered > X tokens.

morgan: thanks team. Follow-up items: RCA (ravi), runbook update (lia), PR for ramp guard (devon), customer comms update (morgan). Handoff complete."
